is_anopheles.evidence: The study tests Anopheles arabiensis and Anopheles funestus (page 1, Title and Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study does not genotype any resistance markers. It only cites previous literature regarding the presence of L1014F in the SENN-DDT colony (page 2, 'Methods: Mosquito strains').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies are generated or reported; only phenotypic bioassay mortality data across different temperatures are tested.

african_field_population.evidence: All experiments were performed exclusively using long-established laboratory colonies: SENN (maintained since 1990), SENN-DDT, FUMOZ (maintained since 2000), and FUMOZ-R (page 2, 'Methods: Mosquito strains'). No field-collected mosquitoes were used.

is_primary_study.evidence: The paper is a primary experimental laboratory bioassay study assessing temperature effects on insecticide toxicity.

sub_country_location.evidence: Not applicable to field populations as only long-term laboratory colonies were evaluated.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Not applicable to field populations as only laboratory colonies were tested.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard experimental study on established laboratory colonies.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary Table S1 only contains sample sizes and environmental conditions for bioassay tests; no genotype data exists.

assessment.summary: This laboratory study evaluated the effect of temperature (18, 25, and 30 deg C) on deltamethrin and bendiocarb toxicity, as well as PBO synergism, using colonized Anopheles arabiensis (SENN, SENN-DDT) and Anopheles funestus (FUMOZ, FUMOZ-R) strains. No field mosquitoes were tested and no resistance marker genotyping was performed.
exclusion_reasons: No target resistance markers were genotyped.
Mosquitoes tested were exclusively colonized laboratory strains (SENN, SENN-DDT, FUMOZ, FUMOZ-R); no African field-collected populations were evaluated.
